title: LIA: A Single-GPU LLM Inference Acceleration with Cooperative AMX-Enabled CPU-GPU Computation and CXL Offloading
problem: Single-GPU LLM inference is constrained by GPU memory capacity, forcing either expensive multi-GPU deployments or frequent CPU-GPU transfers over slow PCIe, which bottleneck both latency and throughput.
motivation: Modern Intel CPUs with Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) achieve 20-40 TFLOPS matrix multiplication throughput—comparable to some GPUs—unlocking significant computation offloading to CPUs to reduce PCIe data movement and GPU memory pressure.
method: LIA is a single-GPU LLM inference framework that systematically offloads matrix computations to AMX-enabled CPUs (4th-gen Sapphire Rapids and 6th-gen Granite Rapids Xeon), reducing CPU-GPU transfers by keeping model parameters near the CPU. LIA introduces a memory-offloading policy that integrates CXL memory (as an affordable DRAM extension) with DDR memory to expand effective model capacity for throughput-oriented batch workloads. The system partitions transformer layer computations between CPU and GPU based on runtime latency/throughput objectives, using AMX tile instructions for high-throughput GEMM on the CPU side.
key_novelty: A cooperative CPU-GPU inference framework that exploits AMX matrix extensions on modern Intel CPUs as a genuine compute peer to the GPU, combined with CXL memory integration for extended model capacity without multi-GPU cost.
contributions: Benchmarking of AMX throughput on Sapphire Rapids (20 TFLOPS) and Granite Rapids (40 TFLOPS), demonstrating viability as GPU-class compute for LLM offloading.
LIA framework for cooperative AMX-enabled CPU-GPU LLM inference with latency and throughput optimization.
CXL memory offloading policy integrated with DDR to enable larger batch sizes (up to 900-1.6K) and 1.5x additional throughput.
Up to 19x lower latency and 5.1x higher throughput vs state-of-the-art single-GPU offloading on Granite Rapids + H100.

metrics.speedup: Up to 5.1x lower latency (Sapphire Rapids), up to 19x lower latency (Granite Rapids) vs latest single-GPU offloading; 3.7x-5.1x higher throughput
metrics.other: CXL offloading yields additional 1.5x throughput; max batch size increased 1.8x (900-1.6K)

baselines: LIA with DDR memory only (for CXL comparison)
limitations: Not discussed; cost and availability of CXL memory hardware and Granite Rapids systems in production deployments are not addressed.
primary_theme: AMX CPU-GPU cooperative LLM inference with CXL memory offloading
